Polar Coordinate Fourier Volume Rendering (Polar FVR) is a domain-transform volume rendering method that stores and processes frequency domain data in polar coordinates to reduce computational complexity from $O(n^2 \log n)$ to $O(n^2)$ and improve memory access efficiency [S1].

The claim states that Polar FVR is a domain-transform volume rendering method that stores and processes frequency domain data in polar coordinates to reduce computational complexity from O(n^2 log n) to O(n^2) and improve memory access efficiency. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms all these points: it describes the method as storing/processing frequency domain data in polar coordinates, states that the complexity is reduced to O(n^2) from O(n^2 log n), and explains that storing data along the radial direction ensures adjacent memory access, making memory access more efficient.
